sources.citation: Pavlov, I. P. (1927). Conditioned Reflexes: An Investigation of the Physiological Activity of the Cerebral Cortex (G. V. Anrep, Trans. & Ed.). London: Oxford University Press. Lecture II read in full (Classics in the History of Psychology, York University).
sources.notes: URL fetched 2026-10-24 and read. Source of: duct-relocation surgery (parotid to cheek / submaxillary under chin), glass funnel fixed with Mendeleev cement, hemispherical bulb + horizontal graduated tube with coloured fluid, electric drop recorder; drops counted only in earliest period before experimenter separation; metronome demo (secretion after 9 s, 11 drops in 45 s); sound paired with food; Krestovnikov order experiments (electric bell after food: no reflex after 374 combinations; buzzer before food: reflex after 1 combination; vanillin after acid 427 times failed, amyl acetate before acid worked after 20); experimenter blinking/breathing disturbed dogs; special lab funded by a Moscow businessman with isolating trench, cross-shaped corridor, 4 rooms per floor, animal vs experimenter compartments, electrical/pneumatic transmission; conditioned reflexes = new connections in the cerebral hemispheres, likened to education, habits, training. Lecture III also fetched (no 'meat powder' wording found).

sources.citation: Pavlov, I. P. (2010). Conditioned reflexes: An investigation of the physiological activity of the cerebral cortex. Annals of Neurosciences, 17(3), 136-141 (reprint of the 1927 Anrep translation excerpt).

sources.citation: Pavlov, I. P. (1906). The scientific investigation of the psychical faculties or processes in the higher animals. Science, 24(620), 613-619.
sources.notes: Crossref verify_doi: verified=True, 1906, Science, Ivan P. Pavlov. Pavlov's early English-language account of the new research programme (2 years after the Nobel). Used for chronology only; full text not re-read in this pass.

Nobel Lecture 12 December 1904 'Physiology of Digestion' (title per nobelprize.org link in Wikipedia external links).

sources.citation: Todes, D. P. (1997). From the machine to the ghost within: Pavlov's transition from digestive physiology to conditional reflexes. American Psychologist, 52(9), 947-955.
sources.notes: Crossref verified (1997, American Psychologist, Daniel P. Todes). Historian's account of how 'psychic secretion' in the digestion lab led Pavlov to conditional reflexes. Abstract content checked via secondary summary only.

sources.citation: Todes, D. P. (1997). Pavlov's Physiology Factory. Isis, 88(2), 205-246.
sources.notes: Crossref verified (1997, Isis, Daniel P. Todes). How Pavlov's lab ran like a factory with many co-workers; context for 'assistants' scenes. Book-length versions: Todes, Pavlov's Physiology Factory (Johns Hopkins UP, 2002) and Ivan Pavlov: A Russian Life in Science (Oxford UP, 2014, ISBN 978-0-19-992519-3) - not read directly.

sources.citation: Thomas, R. K. (1997). Correcting some Pavloviana regarding 'Pavlov's bell' and Pavlov's 'mugging'. The American Journal of Psychology, 110(1), 115-125.
sources.notes: Crossref verified (1997, Am J Psychol, Roger K. Thomas). Core paper of the 'Pavlov's bell' debate. Wikipedia summary (SRC_WIKI_PAVLOV) reports Littman (1994, Psycoloquy) doubting bell use and Thomas (1994, Psycoloquy 5(80)) finding 'three additional references to Pavlov's use of a bell'. Dossier therefore treats the bell as debated, not as never used.

sources.citation: Rescorla, R. A. (1988). Pavlovian conditioning: It's not what you think it is. American Psychologist, 43(3), 151-160.
sources.notes: Crossref verified. Modern view: conditioning is learning relations among events (what predicts what), not mere contiguity of two stimuli. Used for longform chapter 6 and the misconception 'just pairing'.

sources.citation: Clark, R. E. (2004). The classical origins of Pavlov's conditioning. Integrative Physiological & Behavioral Science, 39(4), 279-294.
sources.notes: Crossref verified (2004, Robert E. Clark). Historical review of how the conditioning work developed; used for longform context only.

sources.citation: Watson, J. B., & Rayner, R. (1920). Conditioned emotional reactions. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 3(1), 1-14.
sources.notes: Crossref verified. 'Little Albert' fear-conditioning study; everyday hook for phobias. Ethically and methodologically criticised; mention only with that caveat.

sources.citation: Gorn, G. J. (1982). The effects of music in advertising on choice behavior: A classical conditioning approach. Journal of Marketing, 46(1), 94-101.
sources.notes: Crossref verified. Advertising hook (liked music paired with a pen colour). Must be paired with SRC_KELLARIS1989.

sources.citation: Kellaris, J. J., & Cox, A. D. (1989). The effects of background music in advertising: A reassessment. Journal of Consumer Research, 16(1), 113-118.
sources.notes: Crossref verified. Reassessment / failed replication of Gorn 1982 - keeps the advertising hook honest.

sources.citation: Proctor, G. B., & Carpenter, G. H. (2007). Regulation of salivary gland function by autonomic nerves. Autonomic Neuroscience, 133(1), 3-18.
sources.notes: Crossref verified. Modern anatomy anchor for the single brain clip: salivation is driven by autonomic nerves from salivary nuclei in the brainstem (matches anatomy_map 'brainstem': automatic reflexes like salivation).

sources.citation: LeDoux, J. E. (2000). Emotion circuits in the brain. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 23, 155-184.
sources.notes: Crossref verified. Fear conditioning via the amygdala - longform chapter on phobias only; deliberately NOT used in the Short (Pavlov's experiment is appetitive salivary conditioning).

sources.citation: Wikipedia contributors. Ivan Pavlov (raw wikitext, revision 1375148285).
sources.notes: Tertiary pointer only. Used for: born 1849 Ryazan, died 1936; invited to the Institute of Experimental Medicine in 1891; conditional reflex developed with assistant Ivan Tolochinov in 1901 ('reflex at a distance', Helsinki 1903, citing Todes 2002); Madrid 14th International Medical Congress 1903 paper 'The Experimental Psychology and Psychopathology of Animals'; bell debate (Littman 1994; Thomas 1994; Catania).
